To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the MOS weak-inversion transconductance amplifier can be linearized by replacing the tail-current source with a MOS transistor biased in the weak inversion triode region; (2) the linearized transconductance can then be kept constant to better than +/- 5% for input voltage variations up to 130mV; (3) this linearized transconductors can be used to design low-power low-frequency filters; (4) the third-order transconductors-C filter

a weak-inversion differential-pair transconductor can be linearized by replacing its tail current source by a MOSFET operating in the triode region and that the linearization is sufficient for a low-power MOS transconductance-C filter to have a dynamic range of more than 60 dB. In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of a low power, high performance, and small area MOS bandpass filter for VLSI applications.
the design of a low-power, high-frequency, low-noise, low-power MOS transconductance-C filter for use in low-power, high-density VLSI.
the development and design of low-voltage, low-power analog circuits for VLSI systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the linearized MOS differential pair is a very promising candidate for the design of low-power integrated filters.
the linearized differential pairs with spoilt current source are very useful in low-power MOS integrated filter applications.
the linearized transconductance-C filter is a viable candidate for use as a low-voltage, low-power, and low-noise bandpass filter for use in portable and battery-operated systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MOS weak-inversion transconductance amplifier is a very promising building block for low-power MOS VLSI filters.
the MOS weak-inversion linearized transconductor is a very attractive alternative to the bipolar transconductors in integrated low-power low-frequency filter applications.
MOS transconductors with spoiled current sources are a good choice for low-voltage low-power applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MOS weak-inversion transconductance stages with spoilt current-sources can be used in analog circuits to achieve a high dynamic range at low supply voltages and low power consumption.
linearized MOS transconductors can be designed with a small area, low power consumption and high dynamic range.
the use of a triode-biased MOSFET in place of a current source is a very powerful technique for linearization.
